text:
maya: Quick question about demote semantics — when we move a prefix from RESIDENT -> SOFT_EVICT, what guarantees do we need for in-flight reads that might rely on the KV lease? :thinking:

jonathan: Good catch. I think we currently (impl) flip residency bit then start eviction timer. But leases are separate; if a request holds a lease it should be allowed to finish. Problem is the read path assumes residency for low-latency prefetch; after demote we might miss and fall back which is ok but we must not corrupt cached metadata.

ravi: Right — the race is: request A reads while demote flips state, request B acquires new lease for same prefix and evicts entries, A then writes back stale metadata. Need to prevent stale-writes and double-free.

sasha: Proposed rules: 1) demote should attach a demote-token tied to the current lease epoch. 2) any in-flight reader that started before demote can finish; but writers must CAS on epoch. 3) eviction only proceeds when outstanding-reader-count == 0 OR demote TTL expires.

maya: That sounds like a strong model. How do we represent epoch atomically across nodes? We have sequencer and per-shard lease manager.

jonathan: We could reuse the existing lease-id (64-bit) and bump it on demote. Sequence: 
```
- acquire lease L
- demote: bump lease -> L+1 and mark demote-ts
- readers check lease at start; if lease changes mid-op their commit fails CAS
- eviction observes lease==L+1 and outstanding==0 -> reclaim
```

ravi: CASing metadata on commit is fine but adds churn. Another path: keep soft-evict as a best-effort hint; allow overlapping reads but ensure cleanup uses tombstones and delayed reclamation window (e.g., 5s) to avoid races. Tradeoff: higher mem use vs simpler fast path.

sasha: We need to consider multitenancy: a tenant could pin a prefix via long-lived pinned sessions. Demote should respect pins — either fail demote or convert to queued demote that waits on pin release.

maya: For Dedicated clusters with strict SLOs we prefer deterministic demote (no soft wait). For hosted multi-tenant, delayed reclaim is ok. So maybe make the policy pluggable: DEMOTE_STRATEGY = {blocking|grace|hint}.

jonathan: Agreed. Implementation sketch: add per-prefix fields: {lease_id, pin_count, readers_inflight, demote_state, demote_ts}. Demote flow: if pin_count>0 -> enqueue; else bump lease_id (unless strategy==hint), set demote_state, schedule reclamation when readers_inflight==0 OR demote_ts+grace_elapsed.

ravi: Need metrics: demote_wait_seconds, demote_reclaim_count, demote_forced_evictions. Also expose per-tenant failed_demotes for operator visibility.

sasha: Edge case: what if a reader is stuck (e.g., slow network) and we keep delaying evict? We'll leak memory. So enforce max_grace (configurable default 30s) and a forced-evict path that converts outstanding readers to a downgrade path — they will get fallbacks and re-fetch from origin.

maya: Could we use a two-phase handshake to avoid CAS on hot path? Example: readers fetch meta and attach a read-handle token to a small in-shard vector, eviction checks token vector emptiness. Cheap if in-memory. But we must bound vector growth (shard-local).

jonathan: That has nice perf. But complexity: cross-shard clients + lock-free updates. We can implement as per-shard epoch counters: reader increments counter at start, decrements at end (atomic add/sub). Demote checks counter. Very cheap.

ravi: Ok, so final proposal we can prototype: 
- default DEMOTE_STRATEGY = grace (10s max, bump lease_id).
- readers use atomic inflight counter per-prefix per-shard.
- commit uses CAS on lease_id if writer touched cache entry; if CAS fails writer falls back to origin and retries.
- eviction honors pin_count and max_grace.

maya: Sounds good. Can someone write a short follow-up RFC sketch (constraints, invariants, metrics, config knobs) and a small spike for per-shard inflight counters? I'll pair on testing harness for races. :thumbsup:

jonathan: I'll draft RFC sketch today.

ravi: I'll mock a havoc test that simulates stuck readers and demote frequency.

sasha: I'll add metrics list and a telemetry hook.

evict-bot: reminder: scheduled cleanup job will run at 2235001800 (UTC) — if we change demote timers update job.

maya: thanks all. Leaving notes in the RFC thread.
